chunks: “The Kaaba complained to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, during the interval between Isa and Muhammad, blessings of Allah be upon them both, and it said: ‘My Lord, why have my visitors become few? Why have those who come to me become few?’ So Allah, majestic is His glory, revealed to it: ‘Indeed, I am sending down a new light upon a people who will yearn for you as cattle yearn for their young, and they will be escorted to you as women are escorted to their husbands.’”
Meaning the Ummah of Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله.

key_terms.أُمَّةَ مُحَمَّدٍ: the community of Prophet Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.الْفَتْرَةِ: the interval or gap between two prophetic missions
key_terms.الْكَعْبَةَ: the Kaaba, the sacred House of Allah and focal point of hajj
key_terms.زُوَّارِي: my visitors, those who come to visit
key_terms.نُوراً جَدِيداً: a new light, referring to a new divine guidance or dispensation
key_terms.يَحِنُّونَ: they yearn deeply or long affectionately

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the special relationship between the Kaaba and the Ummah of Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the Kaaba as complaining over the scarcity of its visitors in the period between Nabi Isa and Prophet Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. Allah responds with the promise of a new light and a community that will deeply long for and flock to the Kaaba, referring to the Ummah of Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and highlighting the special bond between this Ummah and hajj.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
"The Kaaba complained to Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, during the period between Isa (as) and Muhammad (sw), saying, 'O Lord (azj), why have my visitors decreased? Why have those who come to me diminished?'
Allah (swt), Glorified and Exalted, revealed to it: 'I will send down a new light upon a people who will long for you as livestock long for their young and who will come to you in procession as brides are escorted to their husbands.'
This refers to the Ummah of Muhammad (sw) (peace and blessings be upon him and his family)."
